subject: mathematics
title: Chance Check Review
objective: Describe real-life outcomes as certain, likely, unlikely, or impossible.
introduction: Milo is reviewing chance with clouds, coins, and a shell jar. Can you identify certain, likely, unlikely, and impossible events?

vocabulary.term: a fair coin can land heads
vocabulary.definition: A coin has two sides, so it can land on heads or tails.

vocabulary.term: a fish breathing on land is impossible
vocabulary.definition: Fish breathe with gills, so breathing on land cannot happen.

vocabulary.term: rain may be likely with dark clouds
vocabulary.definition: When the sky is full of dark clouds, rain is likely to come.

items.prompt: Milo flips a fair coin. Which sentence about a possible outcome is right?

options.text: A stone floats in the air — certain
A fish can breathe on land — possible
A fair coin can land on heads or tails — possible
The sun will rise tomorrow — impossible

items.explanation: A coin has two faces, so landing on heads or tails is possible — a true chance statement. The others pair the wrong chance word with the event.

items.prompt: A bird spreads its wings. Which chance statement is true?

options.text: A bird can fly — possible
A fair die has seven faces — certain
A fish can breathe on land — possible
The sun will rise tomorrow — impossible

items.explanation: A bird flying is possible — birds fly every day. The others misuse the chance words.

items.prompt: A turtle races a much faster rabbit. Which chance statement is correct?

options.text: A turtle beating a rabbit in a race — unlikely
A fair die has seven faces — certain
A fish can breathe on land — possible
A coin tossed once always lands on heads — certain

items.explanation: A rabbit is much faster, so a turtle winning the race is unlikely — the chance word fits.

items.prompt: Milo rolls a fair die. Which statement about its faces is right?

options.text: A car can run on water — possible
A fair die has six possible faces
The moon will rise tonight — impossible
A feather falls upward — likely

items.explanation: A fair die has exactly six faces, so six possible faces is a true statement about chance.

items.prompt: Milo flips a fair coin. Which sentence tells the chance correctly?

options.text: A coin has seven faces — possible
A fair coin can land on heads or tails
A pig can fly — certain
A dog can talk — likely

items.explanation: A coin has two faces, so heads or tails are the only possible results.
